The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So if they commit immorality, then upon them is half the punishment for free married women﴾.

This verse indicates that when slave women commit fornication they are lashed fifty lashes. Another verse has come which indicates, by its generality, that every adulteress is lashed one hundred lashes, namely His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿The adulterer and the adulteress, lash each one of them with one hundred lashes﴾ [an-Nur: 2]. The answer is clear: this verse specifies the verse of "an-Nur", because a general and a specific text do not contradict one another.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 26:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and to guide you to the ways (sunan) of those before you﴾.

This verse, by its apparent meaning, indicates that the law of those before us is law for us. A parallel to it is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [6:90].

Another verse has come which indicates the opposite of that, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For each of you We have made a law (shir'ah) and a path (minhaj)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48], and the manner of reconciling between these is greatly disputed, following the disagreement over the ruling on this question.

The majority of scholars hold that the law of those before us, if it is established by our law, is law for us, unless a proof from our law indicates its abrogation (naskh), because it has been mentioned to us in our law only for the sake of reflection (i'tibar) and action. According to this view, the way of reconciling the two verses is that the meaning of His saying ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a path﴾ is that the laws of the messengers may abrogate a ruling in some of them that existed in others, or add to some of them a ruling that did not exist in others.

So the shir'ah is then either by adding rulings that were not previously prescribed, or by abrogating something that was previously prescribed. Therefore the verse provides no proof that what is established in our law as having been law for those before us, and not abrogated, is not part of our law, because the addition of what did not exist before, or the abrogation of what existed before, are both not the point of dispute.

As for the view of al-Shafi'i and those who agree with him: the law of those before us is not law for us unless there is a text in our law stating that it is prescribed for us.

The way of reconciling according to them is that what is meant by the ways of those before us and by the guidance in His saying ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided﴾ are the foundations of religion (usul al-din), which are monotheism (tawhid), not the practical legal branches (furu' 'ilmiyyah), as evidenced by His saying ﴿For each of you We have made a law and a path﴾, and so on.

But this reconciliation to which the Shafi'is went is refuted by what al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih, in the commentary on Surah Sad, from Mujahid, that he «asked Ibn 'Abbas: From where did you take the prostration in Sad? Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿And among his descendants, David﴾ [6:84], ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾, so David prostrated for it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prostrated for it».

It is known that the prostration of recitation belongs to the branches (furu') and not to the foundations (usul). Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) made clear that the Prophet (ﷺ) prostrated for it following David. I have explained this question thoroughly in my journey (rihlati), so I have abbreviated it here.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 33:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to those with whom your oaths have bound you, give them their share﴾, the verse.

This verse indicates the inheritance of allies (hulafa', sing. hulif, sworn allies) from their allies. Another verse has come which indicates the opposite of that, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those of kinship are closer to one another in the Book of Allah﴾ [al-Anfal: 75].

The answer is that this verse abrogates His saying: ﴿And to those with whom your oaths have bound you﴾, the verse. Its abrogation of it is the truth, contrary to Abu Hanifa and whoever agreed with him in saying that the inheritance of allies remains today if the deceased has no heir.

Some have answered that the meaning of ﴿give them their share﴾ is, that is, of support and aid (al-muwalah wa al-nusrah), and in that case there is no contradiction between them, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those from whom you fear arrogance (nushuz)...﴾ [the verse], in this noble verse He mentioned that nushuz may occur from women, but He did not clarify whether nushuz may occur from men or not. However, He clarified in another place (p-241) that nushuz may also occur from men, and that is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband nushuz or aversion...﴾ [the verse] [an-Nisa': 128]. The root meaning of nushuz in the language (lughah) is elevation (al-irtifa'). Thus the disobedient woman (an-nashiz) is as if she raises herself above the place where her husband lies down with her. In the terminology of the jurists (fuqaha', istilah), it is leaving obedience to the husband. It is as if the man's nushuz is also his elevating himself above the place where the wife is, and his abandoning lying with her. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if it is a good deed, He doubles it﴾, and so on. In this noble verse He did not specify the least amount by which a good deed is multiplied, nor the most, but He did specify in another place that the least by which it is multiplied is ten times its like, and that is His saying: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [al-An'am: 160].

And He specified in another place that the multiplication may reach seven hundredfold, or even more, as Allah wills, and that is His saying: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes﴾, and so on [al-Baqarah: 261], as has already been mentioned.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 42:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them﴾, the verse, according to the three readings, its meaning is that they wish they would be made level with the earth, so that they would become dust like it, according to the most apparent of the opinions. This meaning is clarified by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when a man will look at what his hands have sent forth, and the disbeliever will say, "Oh, I wish I were dust!"﴾ [An-Naba': 40].

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾. He explained in another place that the non-concealment mentioned here is only with regard to the reporting of their hands and feet of everything they did when a seal is placed upon their mouths, when they deny their polytheism and their sins. This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This Day We seal upon their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65]. Thus His saying, ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ [An-Nisa': 42], does not contradict His saying about them: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [Al-An'am: 23], nor His saying about them also: ﴿We did not used to do any evil﴾ [An-Nahl: 28], nor His saying about them: ﴿Rather, we had not been calling upon anything before﴾ [Ghafir: 74], due to the explanation we have mentioned. And Allah, Exalted is He, knows best.

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾.

(p-253) This verse indicates that the disbelievers will not conceal any part of their account on the Day of Resurrection, and other verses have come indicating the opposite, such as His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists"﴾ [Al-An'am: 23], and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they will offer submission, "We did not used to do any evil"﴾ [An-Nahl: 28].

And His saying: ﴿Rather, we had not been calling upon anything before﴾ [Ghafir: 74].

The manner of reconciling this is what Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, explained when he was asked about His saying, ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ alongside His saying, ﴿And they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾. He said: their tongues will say, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists," so Allah will seal their mouths, and their hands and feet will testify to what they used to do.

Thus they conceal the truth with regard to the tongue and do not conceal it with regard to the hands and feet. This reconciliation is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿This Day We seal upon their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will testify to what they used to earn﴾ [Ya-Sin: 65].

Some scholars answered by the multiplicity of situations: they conceal at one time and do not conceal at another time. And Allah, Exalted is He, knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾. In this verse, Allah, may He be exalted, has explained that the cessation of intoxication (sukr) is that the intoxicated person's intellect returns to him, so that he knows the meaning of the speech that comes from him, by His saying: ﴿until you know what you are saying﴾ [An-Nisa: 43].

(p-242) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Book, how they purchase error and desire that you should lose the way?﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse He mentions that those who were given a portion of the Book, along with their purchasing of error, also desire to misguide the Muslims.

Elsewhere He mentions that they are numerous, and that they wish for the Muslims to revert (to disbelief), and that the cause driving them to this is nothing but envy, and that this came from them only after they had recognized the truth. This is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Many of the People of the Book wish they could turn you back into disbelievers after your belief, out of envy from themselves, after the truth has become clear to them﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109].

Elsewhere He mentions that this misguidance which they wish for the Muslims does not befall the Muslims, but rather it befalls those who wish it, namely (it befalls) them. This is His saying: ﴿A group of the People of the Book wish they could mislead you, but they mislead none except themselves, and they do not perceive﴾ [Al 'Imran: 69].

The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath﴾. He did not explain here the manner of His cursing the companions of the Sabbath. However, He explained in another place that His cursing of them was their transformation (maskh) into apes, and whoever Allah transforms into an ape in anger is undoubtedly accursed. This is His saying: ﴿And you have already known those among you who transgressed concerning the Sabbath, so We said to them, "Be apes, despised and expelled"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 65], and His saying: ﴿So when they persisted in defiance of what they had been forbidden, We said to them, "Be apes, despised and expelled"﴾ [al-A'raf: 166]. The argument that cursing is distinct from transformation, based on its being conjoined to it in His saying: ﴿Say, "Shall I inform you of something worse than that as a recompense from Allah? Those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and swine"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60], establishes no more than that cursing is distinct from transformation in that verse, as al-Alusi stated in his Tafsir, and this is clear. In the language, the curse (al-la'nah) means expulsion and removal. A man whom his people expelled and removed because of his crimes is called by the Arabs "a cursed man (rajul la'in)." From this is the saying of the poet:

*I startled the sand grouse with him and drove away from him the place of the wolf, like the cursed man.*

In the technical usage of the Sharia, the curse (al-la'nah) is expulsion and removal from the mercy of Allah. It is known that transformation is among the greatest kinds of expulsion and removal.

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on Surah 4, verse 48:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.﴾ (p. 243) In this noble verse He mentions that He does not forgive associating partners with Him, that He forgives other than that for whomever He wills, and that whoever associates partners with Him has fabricated a tremendous sin.

In other places He mentions that the condition under which He does not forgive associating partners with Him is when the polytheist does not repent of that. If he repents, He forgives him.

- As in His saying: ﴿except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], where the exception (istithna', the grammatical exception introduced by *illa*, "except") refers back

- to His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke along with Allah another deity﴾ [al-Furqan: 68], and what is conjoined to it, because the meaning of all of it is gathered in His saying: ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [al-Furqan: 68].

- And His saying: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, if they desist, they will be forgiven what has already occurred﴾ [al-Anfal: 38].

In another place He mentions that whoever associates partners with Allah has strayed far from the truth, and this is His saying in this same noble surah as well: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whomever He wills. And whoever associates partners with Allah has strayed into far error﴾ [al-Nisa': 116]. He also explicitly stated that for whoever associates partners with Allah, Paradise is forbidden to him and his abode is the Fire:

- by His saying: ﴿Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah, Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire﴾ [5],

- and His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise, "Pour upon us some water or some of what Allah has provided you." They will say, "Indeed, Allah has forbidden both to the disbelievers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 50].

In another place He mentions that the polytheist has no hope of deliverance, and this is His saying: ﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him away, or the wind carried him off to a distant place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31]. In another place He explicitly stated that associating partners is a tremendous wrong, in His saying, quoting Luqman while affirming it: ﴿Indeed, association with Allah is a tremendous wrong﴾ [Luqman: 13].

In another place He mentioned that complete security and guidance belong only to those who do not mix their faith with polytheism, and this is His saying: ﴿Those who believed and did not mix their belief with wrongdoing (*zulm*) — those will have security, and they are guided﴾ [al-An'am: 82]. It has been authentically related from him (ﷺ) that the meaning of *bi-zulm* ("with wrongdoing") is *bi-shirk* ("with polytheism").

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, and so on. In this verse, Allah, exalted is He, denounced their claiming purity for themselves by His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who...﴾ [al-Nisa': 49], and by His saying: ﴿See how they invent lies against Allah, and sufficient is that as a manifest sin﴾ [al-Nisa': 50]. He explicitly forbade, in general terms, the claiming of purity for oneself, and [by implication] it applies all the more to the soul of the disbeliever, which is the basest and most impure of things, by His saying: ﴿He knows you best, since He produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who has taken heed﴾ [al-Najm: 32]. (p-244) However, He did not here explain the manner in which they claimed purity for themselves.

But He explained that in other places, such as His saying about them: ﴿We are the children of Allah and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18], and His saying: ﴿And they say: None will enter Paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and other verses besides these.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We will admit them to dense shade﴾. In this noble verse He describes the shade of Paradise as *dhaliil* (dense). In another verse He describes it as *daa'im* (perpetual), namely His saying: ﴿Its fruit is perpetual, and its shade﴾ [al-Ra'd: 35]. In another verse He describes it as *mamduud* (extended), namely His saying: ﴿And in extended shade﴾ [56]. In another place He clarified that they are many shades, namely His saying: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in shades and springs﴾ up to the end of the verse [al-Mursalat: 41].

In another place He mentioned that they, in those shades, recline with their spouses on *al-araa'ik* (the couches), namely His saying: ﴿They and their spouses are in shade, reclining on couches﴾ [Ya-Sin: 56]. *Al-araa'ik* is the plural of *arika*, which is the couch set within the *hajala* (a canopied bridal chamber), and the *hajala* is a chamber adorned for the bride with every kind of adornment. He also made clear that the shade of the people of the Fire is not like this, by His saying: ﴿Proceed to that which you used to deny﴾ ﴿Proceed to a shadow having three branches﴾ ﴿Neither cooling nor protecting from the flame﴾ [al-Mursalat: 29–30], and His saying: ﴿And the companions of the left, what are the companions of the left?﴾ ﴿In scorching wind and boiling water﴾ ﴿And shade of black smoke﴾ ﴿Neither cool nor pleasant﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 41–44].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you dispute over anything, refer it back to Allah﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse Allah commands that every matter over which people dispute, whether among the foundations of the religion (usul al-din) or its branches (furu'), must be referred back to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. This is because He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [An-Nisa: 80]. He clarified this command here by His saying: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its judgement is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura: 10]. From this noble verse it is understood that it is not permissible to seek judgement from other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ. He, may He be exalted, has clarified this understanding, rebuking those who seek judgement from other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ, and explaining that Satan has led them far astray from the truth, by His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to seek judgement before the taghut, while they have been commanded to reject it? And Satan intends to lead them far astray﴾ [An-Nisa: 60]. He also indicated that no one believes until he rejects the taghut, by His saying: ﴿So whoever rejects the taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most reliable handhold﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 256].

The implication of the condition is that whoever does not reject the taghut has not grasped the most reliable handhold, and this is so. Whoever does not grasp the most reliable handhold is far removed from faith, because faith in Allah is the most reliable handhold, and faith in the taghut cannot be combined with faith in Allah, because rejecting the taghut is a condition of faith in Allah or a pillar of it, as is clear from His saying: ﴿So whoever rejects the taghut﴾ — the verse [Al-Baqarah: 256].

Caution

Those who deny analogy (qiyas) have used this noble verse, namely His saying: ﴿And if you dispute over anything, refer it back to Allah﴾ — the verse, as evidence for the invalidity of analogy. They said: He has made referral obligatory only to the specific Book and Sunnah, not to analogy. The majority (al-jumhur) answered that there is no proof for them in the verse, because attaching what is not explicitly stated to what is explicitly stated, due to the existence of the meaning of the text in it, does not depart from referral to the Book and the Sunnah. Rather, some of them said: the verse includes all the legal evidences. So obeying Allah means acting upon the Book, obeying the Messenger means acting upon the Sunnah, and referring to both means analogy, because referring a disputed matter that is not known from the text to what is explicitly stated only occurs through comparison and building upon it, and analogy is nothing beyond that.

It is known from His saying: ﴿And if you dispute﴾ that when there is no dispute, one acts upon what is agreed upon, which is consensus (ijma'). This was stated by al-Alusi in his Tafsir.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 61:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion.﴾ In this noble verse, He mentions that when the hypocrites are called to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger ﷺ, they turn away from that with aversion (ṣudūd), meaning they turn away with avoidance (i'rāḍ).

He mentions in another place that when they are called to him ﷺ so that he may seek forgiveness for them, they turn their heads aside, turn away, and act arrogantly. This is His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will seek forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 5]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 65:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves, and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided, and submit in full submission.﴾ In this noble verse, Exalted is He swears by His own noble and sacred Self that no one truly believes until they make His Messenger ﷺ judge in all matters, and then submit to what he has decided, both outwardly and inwardly, and surrender to him with complete submission, without resistance, opposition, or dispute. In another verse He made clear that the saying of the believers is confined to this complete submission and full compliance, both outwardly and inwardly, to what he ﷺ has decided, and that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The only saying of the believers, when they are called to Allah and His Messenger that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey."﴾ [al-Nur: 51], and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 72:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But if a calamity strikes you, he says, "Allah has certainly blessed me, for I was not present with them as a witness."﴾ In this noble verse, He mentions that the hypocrites (munafiqin), when they hear that a calamity has befallen the Muslims, that is, the killing of them by the enemies, or wounds that struck them, or the like, say: their absence from them is one of the blessings of Allah upon them.

He mentions in other places that they rejoice at the evil that befalls the Muslims, as in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If a good thing befalls you, it distresses them; but if an evil befalls you, they rejoice at it﴾ [Al 'Imran: 120], and His saying: ﴿If a calamity befalls you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution before," and they turn away while they are rejoicing﴾ [At-Tawbah: 50].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 73:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah should reach you, he would surely say, as if there had never been between you and him any affection, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have achieved a great achievement."﴾ In this noble verse, He mentions that when the hypocrites hear that a bounty from Allah has reached the Muslims, that is, victory, triumph, and spoils of war, they wish they had been with them, so that they too might gain their share of the spoils.

He mentions in other places that this bounty which reaches the believers distresses them because of their intense inner enmity towards them, as in His saying: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them﴾ [Al 'Imran: 120], and His saying: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 50].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or is victorious﴾ [the verse], He mentions in this noble verse that He will surely give the one who strives in His way a great reward, whether he is killed in the way of Allah or overcomes his enemy and gains victory over him.

And He explains in another place that both states are "husna" (the best outcome), namely His saying: ﴿Say: Do you await for us except one of the two best outcomes?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 52]. And "husna" is a superlative form, since it is the feminine of "al-ahsan" (the best).

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 78:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab [Removing the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book]):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," but if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you [O Muhammad]." Say, "All is from Allah."﴾

There is no contradiction between it and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah, and whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾ [An-Nisa: 79].

The answer is clear: the meaning of His saying ﴿And if good befalls them﴾, that is, rain, fertility, provision and well-being, "they say, 'This is what Allah has blessed us with,'" and ﴿if evil befalls them﴾, that is, drought, famine, poverty and sickness, "they say, 'This is from you'", that is, "from your ill omen, O Muhammad, and the ill omen of what you have brought." Say to them: "All of that is from Allah."

It is known that Allah is the One who brings the rain, provision and well-being, just as He brings drought, famine, poverty, sickness and calamities. A parallel to this verse is Allah's saying about Pharaoh and his people with Musa (p-254): ﴿And if evil befalls them, they say, "This is due to Musa and those with him"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 131].

And His saying, exalted is He, about the people of Salih with Salih: ﴿They said, "We have taken an omen from you and those with you"﴾ [An-Naml: 47], and the saying of the people of the town to the messengers who were sent to them: they said, ﴿"Indeed, we take omens from you. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you"﴾ [Ya-Sin: 18].

As for His saying: ﴿Whatever good reaches you is from Allah﴾, that is, because He is the One who bestows every blessing. ﴿And whatever evil reaches you is from yourself﴾, that is, from your side and from the side of your own deeds, since evil does not befall a person except through what his hands have earned, as Allah said: ﴿And whatever misfortune strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

The explanation of this matter, concerning the question of the actions of servants, which removes the difficulty, will come, God willing, in surah "Ash-Shams", in the discussion of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He inspired it with its wickedness and its righteousness﴾ [Ash-Shams: 8]. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

In this verse, He restricted the slave to be freed in the expiation for accidental killing by faith, and He left the slave in the expiation for zihar and oaths unrestricted from the condition of faith, since He said in each of them: ﴿then freeing a slave﴾ and did not say "a believing [slave]."

This issue is one of the issues of the conflict between the unrestricted (mutlaq) and the restricted (muqayyad). The summary of the explanation of this matter is that the unrestricted and the restricted have four states:

The first: that their ruling and their cause are the same, such as the verse of blood, whose discussion has preceded. The majority of scholars apply the unrestricted to the restricted in this state, which is the unity of cause and ruling together. This is one of the methods of the Arabic language, for they mention and then omit, relying on what was mentioned. Like the saying of the poet, who is Qays ibn al-Khatim:

"We are content with what we have, and you are content with what you have, and opinions differ."

He omitted "radun" (content) because "radin" (content) indicates it. A similar example is also the saying of Dabi' ibn al-Harith al-Burjumi:

"Whoever has his saddle-bag in Medina, then I and Qayyar are strangers there.
He threw at me a matter of which I and my father were innocent, and he threw me for the sake of al-Tawi."

Some scholars said: applying the unrestricted to the restricted is by analogy (qiyas), and it was said by reason ('aql), which is the weakest of them. And Allah knows best.

The second state: that the ruling is the same and the cause differs, as in this verse, where the ruling is one, namely freeing a slave, and the cause differs, namely accidental killing and zihar for example. Such an unrestricted term is applied to the restricted according to the Shafi'is, the Hanbalis and many of the Malikis. For this reason they required faith in the expiation of zihar, applying the unrestricted to the restricted, contrary to Abu Hanifa. What indicates the application of this unrestricted to the restricted is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ in the story of Mu'awiya ibn al-Hakam al-Sulami: "Free her, for she is a believer," and he did not ask him whether it was an expiation or not. Omitting to ask for specification takes the place of generality in statements. In Maraqi al-Su'ud it is said:

"And let the omission of specification take the place of generality in statements."

The third state: the reverse of this, namely the unity of cause with difference of ruling. It was said that the unrestricted is applied to the restricted in it, and it was said no, and this is the view of most scholars. An example is fasting for zihar and feeding (the poor) for zihar. Their cause is one, namely zihar, but their ruling differs, because this is fasting and that is feeding, and one of them is restricted by consecutiveness, which is fasting, while the second is unrestricted from the condition of consecutiveness, which is feeding. So this unrestricted is not applied to that restricted.

Those who hold that the unrestricted is applied to the restricted in this state gave as an example feeding for zihar, for it was not restricted to being before the two touch, although its freeing and its fasting were restricted by His saying: ﴿before they touch one another﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 3]. So this unrestricted is applied to the restricted, and feeding must be before intercourse.

Al-Lakhmi gave as an example feeding in the expiation of oaths, where it is restricted by His saying: ﴿from the average of what you feed your families﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 89].

And clothing was left unrestricted from that restriction when He said: ﴿or clothing them﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 89]. So the unrestricted is applied to the restricted, and it is required that the clothing be from the average of what you clothe your families with.

The fourth state: that they differ in both ruling and cause together, and there is no application (of one to the other) by consensus, and this is clear. This applies when the restricted term is one.

(p-256) But if two restricted terms come with two different restrictions, it is not possible to apply the unrestricted to both of them, because their restrictions conflict. Rather, one looks at them: if one of them is closer to the unrestricted than the other, the unrestricted is applied to the closer of the two according to a group of scholars, and so it is restricted by its restriction. If neither of them is closer to it, it is restricted by neither of them, and it remains on its generality, because preferring without a preference is impossible.

An example of one of them being closer to the unrestricted than the other is the fast of the expiation of oaths: it is unrestricted from the condition of consecutiveness or separation, while the fast of zihar is restricted to consecutiveness and the fast of tamattu' is restricted to separation. The oath is closer to zihar than tamattu' is, because each of the oath and zihar is a fast of expiation, unlike the fast of tamattu'. So the fast of the expiation of oaths is restricted to consecutiveness according to those who hold that, and it is not restricted to the separation found in the fast of tamattu'.

The reading of Ibn Mas'ud, "then a fast of three days, consecutively (mutatabi'at)," is not established, because the Companions agreed on not writing "mutatabi'at" in the Mushaf. An example of the two being such that neither is closer to the unrestricted than the other is the fast of making up Ramadan, for Allah said of it: ﴿then an equal number of other days﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 184], and He did not restrict it to consecutiveness or separation, even though He restricted the fast of zihar to consecutiveness and the fast of tamattu' to separation, and neither of them is closer to the making up of Ramadan than the other. So it is not restricted by either of them; rather it remains a matter of choice: if one wishes, one may make it consecutive, and if one wishes, one may separate it. And knowledge is with Allah, exalted is He.

Allah's statement: ﴿Urge the believers﴾ [An-Nisa: 84], and so on. Here He did not state explicitly what the believers are to be urged to, but He stated it in another place, that it is fighting (qital), namely His saying: ﴿Urge the believers to fight﴾. He alluded to this here by His saying at the beginning of the verse: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah﴾, and His saying at its end: ﴿It may be that Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve﴾, and so on.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 88:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And whoever Allah sends astray, you will never find for him a way.﴾ In this noble verse, Allah, exalted is He, rebukes those who wish to guide the one whom Allah has sent astray, and He explicitly states therein that for whomever Allah has sent astray, there is no path (sabil) to his guidance. He clarified this meaning in many verses, such as His saying: ﴿And whoever Allah intends for his trial, you will not avail him anything against Allah. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah did not intend to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41], and His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah sends astray, there is none to guide him.﴾ [al-A'raf: 186]. It is derived from these verses that the servant should greatly beseech and entreat Allah, exalted is He, to guide him and not to let him go astray, for whomever Allah guides does not go astray, and whomever He sends astray has no guide. Therefore, He mentioned of those firmly grounded in knowledge (al-Rasikhun fi al-'ilm, those deeply rooted in knowledge) that they say: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 8], the verse.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 93:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever, and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ — the verse.

This verse indicates that one who kills intentionally has no repentance, and that he is abiding forever in the Fire. Other verses have come that indicate otherwise, such as His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that a partner be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa: 116].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right﴾ — up to His saying — ﴿except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ — the verse [Al-Furqan: 70].

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾ [Az-Zumar: 53].

(p-257) And His saying: ﴿And indeed, I am Forgiving to one who repents, believes﴾ — the verse [Al-Furqan: 82].

To reconcile these, there are several aspects. Among them: His saying ﴿his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever﴾ means: if he considers the killing of a believer intentionally permissible, because one who deems that lawful is a disbeliever.

This was said by Ikrimah and others, and what supports it is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Jubayr, and Ibn Jarir from Ibn Juraij, that it was revealed concerning Miqyas ibn Subabah, who embraced Islam along with his brother Hisham, and they were in Medina. Miqyas found his brother slain among the Banu al-Najjar, and did not know his killer. The Prophet ﷺ ordered that the blood-money be paid to him, and the Ansar gave him one hundred camels. The Prophet ﷺ sent with him a man from Quraysh from the Banu Fihr. Miqyas then targeted the Fihri, the messenger of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and killed him, apostatized from Islam, mounted one of the camels of the blood-money, and drove the rest with him, and joined Mecca as an apostate. He said in a poem of his:

"I slew for him Fihr, and I carried his blood-money, the chiefs of the Banu al-Najjar, the lords of Fari'."

"I attained my vengeance and lay down, reclining, and I was the first to return to the idols."

This Miqyas is the one concerning whom the Prophet ﷺ said: "I will not grant him security in the sacred area or outside it." He was killed clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah on the day of the Conquest. So the killer who is like Miqyas ibn Subabah, one who deems killing lawful and apostatizes from Islam, there is no doubt regarding his abiding in the Fire.

Based on this, the verse is specific to what resembles its occasion of revelation, by the evidence of the texts explicitly stating that none of the believers will abide forever in the Fire.

The second aspect: the meaning of "his recompense" is that he is requited, while it is possible he would not be requited if he repents, or if he has a righteous deed that outweighs his evil deed. This is the view of Abu Hurayrah, Abu Mijlaz, Abu Salih, and a group of the early generations (salaf).

The third aspect: the verse is for severity in deterrence. This aspect was mentioned by al-Khatib and al-Alusi in their tafsirs, and al-Alusi attributed it to some verifiers, and both argued for it with His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever disbelieves, then indeed Allah is free of need from the worlds﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 97], on the view that its meaning is "and whoever does not perform Hajj."

And with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ, established in the Two Sahihs, to al-Miqdad when he asked him about killing one of the disbelievers who embraced Islam after (p-258) he had cut off his hand in battle: "Do not kill him. If you kill him, then he is in your position before you kill him, and you are in his position before he uttered the word he uttered."

This aspect is of the type of disbelief that is less than disbelief, and abiding that is less than abiding. The apparent meaning of it, according to the one who holds it, is that "abiding" means a long stay, and the Arabs sometimes use the term "abiding" for a long stay. Among this is the saying of Labid:

"I stood asking them, and how is our asking? Deaf, abiding ones, whose speech is not clear."

However, the correct meaning of the verse is the second aspect and the first, and as for the deterrent severity, some scholars interpreted Ibn Abbas's statement that this verse abrogates everything else. And Allah knows best.

The one who edits it, may Allah pardon him, said: What appears is that the one who kills intentionally is a believer who is disobedient and has repentance, as the majority of the scholars of the Ummah hold. This is the explicit statement of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿except one who repents and believes﴾ — the verse. The claim that it is restricted to disbelievers has no evidence. This is also indicated by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾.

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah forgives all sins﴾.

The hadiths have been widely transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ that whoever has in his heart an atom's weight of faith will come out of the Fire.

Allah, may He be exalted, explicitly stated that the killer is the brother of the one killed, in His saying: ﴿But if he is pardoned by his brother, [some] remission⁠﴾ — the verse [Al-Baqarah: 178]. And the brother of a believer is none but a believer. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And if two groups of the believers fight, [make peace]﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 9], so He called them believers although some of them kill others.

Among what indicates this is what is established in the Two Sahihs regarding the story of the Israelite who killed one hundred souls, because this Ummah is more deserving of lightening than the Children of Israel, since Allah removed from it the burdens and the shackles that were upon them.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Not equal are those who sit back among the believers, other than those with a harmful excuse, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit back by a degree. And to each Allah has promised the best reward. Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit back with a great reward.﴾ In this noble verse, He mentioned that He preferred those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives over those who sit back by a degree and a great reward, and He did not address the preference of some strivers over others. However, He explained that in another place, which is His saying: ﴿Not equal are those among you who spent and fought before the conquest. They are greater in degree than those who spent afterward and fought. And to each Allah has promised the best reward.﴾ [al-Hadid: 10]. His saying in this noble verse, ﴿other than those with a harmful excuse﴾, is understood by the implication of its opposite that whoever is held back by an excuse, if his intention is sound, attains the reward of the one who strives.

This implication was explicitly stated by the Prophet (ﷺ) in the authentic hadith of Anas, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, there are people in Madinah who, whenever you traveled any journey or crossed any valley, were with you in it." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, while they are in Madinah?" He said: "Yes, the excuse held them back."

On this meaning the poet said:

[al-Basit]

O you who travel to the Ancient House, you have journeyed with bodies, while we have journeyed with spirits.

We have remained upon an excuse and a measure, and whoever remains upon an excuse has indeed journeyed.

(p-248) Caution

From His saying in this noble verse, ﴿And to each Allah has promised the best reward﴾, it is derived that jihad is a communal obligation (fard kifayah) and not an individual obligation (fard 'ayn); for if those who sit back were abandoning an obligation, that would not be consistent with His true promise to them of the best reward, which is Paradise and abundant reward.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 101 (part 1 of 7):

Allah's saying, ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾, to the end of the verse.

Some scholars said: What is meant by "shortening" (al-qasr) in His saying ﴿that you shorten﴾ in this verse is the shortening of the prayer's manner (kayfiyyah), not its number (kammiyyah). The meaning of shortening its manner is that things are permitted in it which are not permitted in the prayer of security (salat al-amn). For example, some of them pray one rak'ah with the Imam, and the Imam stands still until the other group comes and prays with them the second rak'ah. Also, their praying by gesture (ima'), on foot or on riding animals, and not facing the qiblah. All of this is shortening of the manner of the prayer, and what indicates that this is what is meant by the shortening of its manner is:

His saying, Exalted is He, after it, which follows it explaining it: ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let one group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons﴾ to the end of the verse [an-Nisa': 102]. And His saying: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾ [al-Baqarah: 239]. It is further clarified by His saying here: ﴿And when you are secure, then establish the prayer﴾ [4]. And in the verse of al-Baqarah He said: ﴿And when you are secure, then remember Allah as He has taught you what you did not know﴾ [al-Baqarah: 239]. This is because its meaning is: when you are secure, then complete its manner with its bowing and prostration and all that is required in it which is impossible at the time of fear.

On the basis of this interpretation, which the Qur'an indicates, the condition of fear in His saying ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾ [an-Nisa': 101] is binding. That is: if you do not fear that they will tempt you, then do not shorten its manner, but pray it in the most complete forms, as He stated clearly in His saying: ﴿And when you are secure, then establish the prayer﴾ [4]. He also stated the condition of fear for shortening its manner, by allowing it to be prayed by one who walks or rides, in His saying: ﴿But if you fear, then on foot or riding﴾. Then He said: ﴿And when you are secure, remember Allah as He has taught you﴾, to the end of the verse, meaning: when you are secure, then establish your prayer as I have commanded you, with its bowing and prostration, its standing and sitting, in the most complete and perfect form. The best way to explain the Qur'an is by the Qur'an.

(p-٢٤٩) What also indicates that what is meant by "shortening" in this verse is the shortening of its manner, as we have mentioned, is that al-Bukhari introduced the chapter on the prayer of fear with his words: "Chapter: The Prayer of Fear, and the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Indeed, the disbelievers are to you a clear enemy﴾ ﴿And when you are among them and lead them in prayer, let one group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. And when they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come and pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your belongings so they could attack you in one swift turn. And there is no blame upon you if you put down your weapons because of rain or if you are ill, but take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 101, 102]."

As for what Ibn Hajar and others mentioned, that al-Bukhari cited the two verses in the chapter heading to point out that the prayer of fear departs from the form of the rest of the prayers by the Book in statement and by the Sunnah in action, this does not contradict what we have pointed to, namely that he cited the two verses in the heading to alert that the shortening of manner reported in the hadiths of the chapter is what is meant by the shortening of the prayer in His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾. It is also supported by the fact that shortening the number does not require fear, and the Prophet (ﷺ) himself and his Companions used to shorten the prayer while traveling while they were in complete security, as occurred in the Farewell Pilgrimage and other occasions. And as the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the people of Makkah: "Complete your prayer, for we are a traveling people."

Among those who said that what is meant by "shortening" in this verse is shortening of the manner, not the number, were Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi, as reported from them by Ibn Kathir, and this is also the view of Abu Bakr al-Razi al-Hanafi. Ibn Jarir reported something similar from Ibn Umar. When Ibn Kathir reported this view from those we have mentioned, he said: They relied on what Imam Malik narrated from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "The prayer was prescribed as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs, in travel and at home. Then the prayer of travel was confirmed, and the prayer at home was increased."

This hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari from Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Tinnisi, by Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya, by Abu Dawud from al-Qa'nabi, and by al-Nasa'i from Qutaybah, all four from Malik with this chain. They said: If the original of the prayer in travel is two, then how can "shortening" here mean shortening of the number? Because what is the original does not get described with His saying: ﴿there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer﴾.

Clearer in indicating this is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Waki' and Sufyan and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, (p-٢٥٠) from Zubayd al-Yami, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The prayer of travel is two rak'ahs, the prayer of Eid al-Adha is two rak'ahs, the prayer of Eid al-Fitr is two rak'ahs, and the Friday prayer is two rak'ahs, complete and not shortened, upon the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ)."

Likewise it was narrated by al-Nasa'i, Ibn Majah, and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih through various chains from Zubayd al-Yami with this. This is a chain that meets the conditions of Muslim. Muslim, in the introduction to his book, ruled that Ibn Abi Layla heard from Umar, and it is stated explicitly in this hadith and others. This is the correct view, if Allah wills, although Yahya ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim, and al-Nasa'i said that he did not hear from him.

On this basis as well, he said: It occurred in some chains of Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, through the chain of al-Thawri from Zubayd, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from "a trustworthy man" from Umar, and so he mentioned it. In Ibn Majah's narration through Yazid ibn Ziyad ibn Abi al-Ja'd from Zubayd, from Abd al-Rahman, from Ka'b ibn Ujrah, from Umar. So Allah knows best.

Muslim in his Sahih, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of Abu Awanah al-Wadddah ibn Abd Allah al-Yashkuri (Muslim, al-Nasa'i, and Ayyub ibn A'idh added), both from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Abd Allah ibn Abbas, who said: "Allah prescribed the prayer upon the tongue of your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): four in residence, two in travel, and one in fear. Just as it is prayed in residence before it and after it, so likewise it is prayed in travel."

Ibn Majah also narrated it from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd from Tawus himself. So this is established from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them. It does not contradict what preceded from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, because she informed that "the original prayer was two rak'ahs, but it was increased in the prayer of residence. When that was established, it became correct to say that the obligatory prayer of residence is four," as Ibn Abbas said. And Allah knows best.

However, the hadith of Ibn Abbas and that of Aisha agree that the prayer of travel is two rak'ahs, and that it is complete and not shortened, as is stated explicitly in the hadith of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. Know that the hadith of Aisha mentioned has been criticized from eight angles:

The first: that it is contradicted by consensus (ijma'). Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi al-Maliki said in his book called al-Qabas: "Our scholars said: this hadith is rejected by consensus."

The second: that she herself acted contrary to it, and the transmitter is among the people most knowledgeable about what he narrates. So she, may Allah be pleased with her, (p-٢٥١) used to complete the prayer while traveling. They said: her acting contrary to her own narration weakens the hadith.

The third: the consensus of the jurists of the major cities that it is not a basis to be taken into account for the traveler's prayer behind a resident (muqim).

The fourth: that other Companions opposed it, such as Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: "The prayer was prescribed in residence as four, in travel as two, and in fear as one." We have already cited Muslim's and others' narration of this from Ibn Abbas.

The fifth: the claim that it is irregular (mudtarib), because Ibn Ajlan narrated it from Salih ibn Kaysan, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prescribed the prayer as two rak'ahs." Al-Awza'i narrated it from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, from Aisha, who said: "Allah prescribed the prayer upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs," and so on. They said: this is irregularity.

The sixth: that it is not on its apparent meaning, because the Maghrib and the Subh were not increased nor decreased.

The seventh: that it is a statement of Aisha and not a marfu' (attributed to the Prophet).

The eighth: the statement of Imam al-Haramayn: "If it were authentic, it would have been transmitted by tawatur (mass transmission)."

Its annotator (muqayyiduhu), may Allah pardon him, said: All of these objections raised against the hadith of Aisha are invalid. As for its contradiction by consensus, its invalidity is clear, because no consensus is valid on this point, and Ibn al-Arabi himself mentioned the disagreement on it.

Al-Qurtubi said, after mentioning Ibn al-Arabi's claim of the aforementioned consensus: "I say: this is not valid, for he and others mentioned the disagreement and dispute, so what they claimed of consensus is not established."

As for its contradiction by Aisha's acting against it, this too is clearly invalid, because what matters is her narration, not her opinion, as is the correct view according to the majority. We have explained this in surah al-Baqarah in discussing the hadith of Tawus mentioned earlier in al-Talaq.

As for its contradiction by the consensus of the jurists of the major cities that it is not a basis to be taken into account for the traveler's prayer behind a resident, its answer is that the jurists of the major cities did not agree on that. A group of scholars held that the traveler's following of a resident is not valid, because they differ in number and in intention, and they argued (p-٢٥٢) with the hadith: "Do not differ from your Imam." Among those who held this view were al-Sha'bi, Tawus, Dawud al-Zahiri, and others.

As for its contradiction by the opposition of some Companions to it, such as Ibn Abbas, its answer is what we have just presented from Ibn Kathir, that when the prayer of residence was increased and that became established, it became correct to say: the obligatory prayer of residence is four, as Ibn Abbas said.

As for weakening it by irregularity (idtirab), this is clearly invalid, because there is no irregularity in it at all. The meaning of "Allah prescribed" and "the Messenger of Allah prescribed" is one, because Allah is the Lawgiver and the Messenger is the one who explains. So when it is said "the Messenger of Allah prescribed such-and-such," what is meant is that he conveyed that from Allah, and this does not contradict that it was Allah who prescribed it, as He said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ [an-Nisa': 80]. A parallel to this is the hadith "Indeed Ibrahim made Makkah sacred," together with the hadith "Indeed Allah made Makkah sacred," to the end of the hadith.

As for its rejection on the basis that the Maghrib and the Subh were not increased, this too is clearly invalid, because the intent of the hadith is the prayers that are shortened specifically, as is evident. Moreover, some narrations from Aisha in Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, and al-Bayhaqi say: "The prayer of travel and residence was prescribed as two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah and became settled, two rak'ahs were added to the prayer of residence, and the Fajr prayer was left as it was because of the length of its recitation, and the Maghrib prayer because it is the odd rak'ah of the day." And in Ahmad's narration through Ibn Kaysan in the hadith of Aisha mentioned: "Except the Maghrib, for it was three."

These narrations make clear that the intent is specifically the prayers that are shortened. As for its rejection on the basis that it is not marfu', this is clearly invalid, because it is a matter in which opinion has no place, so it has the ruling of the marfu'. Even if we grant that Aisha did not witness the prescription of the prayer, it is possible that she heard it from the Prophet (ﷺ) during her time with him. And even if we suppose that she did not hear it from him, it is a mursal (report) of a Companion (mursal sahabi), and the mursal reports of the Companions have the ruling of the connected (mawsul) reports.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 101 (part 2 of 7):

As for the statement of Imam al-Haramayn (al-Juwayni) that if it were established it would have been transmitted as mutawatir (widely attested), it is clearly baseless, because the like of this is not rejected on account of a lack of tawatur. Now that you know from what preceded that the prayer of travel was prescribed as two rak'ahs, as the hadith has been authentically reported on the authority of 'A'ishah, Ibn 'Abbas and 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them all, know that Ibn Kathir, after citing the hadith from 'Umar, Ibn 'Abbas and 'A'ishah, said the following:

"If that is the case, then the meaning of His words: ﴿there is no blame upon you﴾ [an-Nisa': 101] is that you shorten the prayer in its manner (qasr al-kayfiyyah), as in the prayer of fear (salat al-khawf). For this reason He said: ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, and the verse. For this reason He said after it: ﴿And when you are among them and establish the prayer for them﴾, and the verse [an-Nisa': 102]. So He clarified the intended meaning of shortening here, and mentioned its description and manner." End of the relevant part of his words. It is very clear in what we have mentioned, and this is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir.

* *

On this view, the verse concerns the prayer of fear, and the shortening of the prayer during travel is derived from the Sunnah, not from the Qur'an. Other views have been stated regarding the meaning of the noble verse:

The first: the meaning of "if you shorten the prayer" ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾ [an-Nisa': 101] is limiting it to one rak'ah in the prayer of fear, as we have mentioned earlier from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in Muslim, an-Nasa'i, Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah, and we mentioned earlier that Ibn Majah narrated it from Tawus.

Abu Dawud and an-Nasa'i narrated something similar from the hadith of Hudhayfah, who said: "He prayed one rak'ah with these and one rak'ah with those, and they did not make up (the prayer)." an-Nasa'i also narrated it from the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit from the Prophet ﷺ.

Among those who held that the prayer of fear is limited to one rak'ah were al-Thawri, Ishaq and those who followed them. It is also reported from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, 'Ata', Jabir, al-Hasan, Mujahid, al-Hakam, Qatadah, Hammad and al-Dahhak.

Some said: the dawn prayer is performed as one rak'ah in fear. This was the view of Ibn Hazm, and it is reported from Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi that the prayer of fear is limited to one rak'ah.

Abu Hurayrah, Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and more than one of the Tabi'un said so, and some restricted it to severe fear.

On this view, the shortening in His words ﴿that you shorten the prayer﴾ [an-Nisa': 101] is qasr al-kammiyyah (shortening in quantity).

A group said: the intended shortening in His words ﴿that you shorten the prayer﴾ is the shortening of the prayer during travel. They said: there is no mafhum al-mukhalafah (implied opposite meaning) in the condition His words ﴿if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾ represent, because it came out in the form of what is usual at the time this verse was revealed, for at the beginning of Islam after the Hijrah most of their journeys were dangerous.

It is established in the principles of jurisprudence that among the impediments to considering mafhum al-mukhalafah is that the statement came out in the form of what is usual. For this reason the majority did not consider mafhum al-mukhalafah in His words ﴿those in your guardianship﴾ [an-Nisa': 23], because it follows what is usual.

In Maraqi al-Su'ud, in mentioning the impediments to considering mafhum al-mukhalafah, he said: [Rajaz meter]
"Or he was ignorant of the ruling, or the utterance was prompted by a question, or it followed what was predominant."

Those who said the verse means shortening the four-rak'ah prayer during travel cited what Muslim in his Sahih, Imam Ahmad, and the authors of the four Sunan narrated from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said: "I said to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: ﴿there is no blame upon you that you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve will attack you﴾, but people are now secure. He said: I was surprised at what you were surprised at, so I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and he said: 'It is a charity which Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity.'"

This hadith, which is established in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, indicates that Ya'la ibn Umayyah and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both, believed that the meaning of the verse is shortening the four-rak'ah prayer during travel, and that the Prophet ﷺ approved of 'Umar's understanding of it. This is strong evidence, but it is opposed by what has preceded from 'Umar, that he said: "The prayer of travel is two rak'ahs, complete and not shortened, upon the tongue of Muhammad ﷺ," and it is supported by the hadith of 'A'ishah and the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas mentioned earlier.

The apparent meaning of the preceding verses, which indicate that His words "that you shorten the prayer" mean the shortening of manner in the prayer of fear, is as we have mentioned, and Allah knows best. The forms of the prayer of fear are many: the enemy may be in the direction of the qiblah or in another direction; the prayer may be four, three or two rak'ahs; then at times they pray in congregation, and at times the fighting becomes intense so that they cannot pray in congregation, but pray individually, on foot or mounted, facing the qiblah or not facing it. All the forms of the prayer of fear reported in the authentic collections are permissible, and their forms and manners are detailed in the books of hadith and jurisprudence. We will mention what the four Imams held concerning them, God willing.

As for Malik ibn Anas, the form he adopted is that the first group prays with the Imam one rak'ah in the two-rak'ah prayer and two rak'ahs in the four- and three-rak'ah prayers, then completes the remainder of the prayer, which is two in the four-rak'ah prayer and one in the two- and three-rak'ah prayers, then they give the salam and stand facing the enemy. The second group comes and finds the Imam standing waiting for them. He has the choice in his standing between recitation, supplication and silence if it is a two-rak'ah prayer, and between supplication and silence if it is a four- or three-rak'ah prayer. It was said: he waits for them in the four- and three-rak'ah prayers sitting, and then leads them in the remainder of the prayer, which is one rak'ah in the two- and three-rak'ah prayers and two rak'ahs in the four-rak'ah prayer, then he gives the salam and they make up what they missed after his salam, which is one rak'ah in the two-rak'ah prayer and two rak'ahs in the four- and three-rak'ah prayers. Thus the outcome of this form is that he prays with the first group one or two rak'ahs, then they complete for themselves and give the salam, and stand facing the enemy; then the other group comes and he prays the remainder with them, gives the salam, and they complete for themselves.

Ibn Yunus said concerning this form that we have mentioned: "The hadith of al-Qasim is more like the Qur'an, and Malik returned to acting upon it." End.

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon him) says: Ibn Yunus means that the hadith which Malik narrated in the Muwatta', from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, in the manner we have mentioned, is the one to which Malik returned and which he finally preferred over what he narrated from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from one who prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Dhat al-Riqa' the prayer of fear, the hadith. The difference between the narration of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad and that of Yazid ibn Ruman is that the narration of Yazid ibn Ruman states that the Prophet ﷺ prayed with the second group the rak'ah that remained of his prayer, then remained seated while they completed for themselves, then gave the salam with them. You know that the narration of al-Qasim in Malik's Muwatta' is that he prays with the second group the remaining rak'ah, then gives the salam, and they complete after his salam for themselves.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr, pointing to the form we have mentioned, which is the narration of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad in Malik's work, said: this is what Malik returned to after he had held the hadith of Yazid ibn Ruman. He chose it and returned to it for analogy with the other prayers: the Imam does not wait for the follower, and the follower only makes up after the Imam's salam. The hadith of al-Qasim which Malik narrated in the Muwatta' is mawquf upon Sahl, but it has the ruling of the marfu', since there is no room for opinion in it. The verified view is that it is a mursal of a Companion, since Sahl was young in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. al-Tabari, Ibn Hibban, Ibn al-Sakan and others determined that the Prophet ﷺ died when Sahl was eight years old. Ibn Hazm claimed that none of the earlier scholars is reported to have held the form we have mentioned, which Malik returned to and narrated in his Muwatta' from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad. This is the summary of Malik's school regarding the manner of the prayer of fear. He first said that the Imam prays with the first group, then they complete for themselves, then they give the salam, then he prays the rest of the prayer with the other group and waits for them until they complete, then he gives the salam with them. He returned to the view that the Imam gives the salam when he has prayed the rest of his prayer with the other group, and does not wait for them until he gives the salam with them, but they complete for themselves after his salam, as we have explained.

The apparent reading is that the indefinite in the narration of Yazid ibn Ruman, in the words of Salih ibn Khawwat, "from one who prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ," the hadith, refers to his father Khawwat ibn Jubayr, the Companion, may Allah be pleased with him, not Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah, as some have said.

The Hafiz said in al-Fath: "But the stronger view is that it is his father Khawwat ibn Jubayr, because Abu Uways narrated this hadith from Yazid ibn Ruman, the teacher of Malik, in it, and said: 'from Salih ibn Khawwat, from his father.' Ibn Mandah narrated it in Ma'rifat al-Sahabah through his chain, and likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it through 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from his father. al-Nawawi in his Tahdhib determined that it was his father Khawwat, and said: it is verified from the narration of Muslim and others." I say: al-Ghazali preceded him in this, for he said that the prayer of Dhat al-Riqa' in the narration of Khawwat ibn Jubayr. End of the relevant passage in his words.

The Malikis did not distinguish between the enemy being in the direction of the qiblah and the enemy being in another direction. As for when the fear becomes intense and the fighting joins, and none of them can abandon the fighting, they pray on foot and mounted, signalling (ima'), facing the qiblah and not facing it, as Allah stated explicitly in His words: ﴿But if you fear, then pray on foot or riding﴾ [al-Baqarah: 239], the verse.

* *

As for al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, he chose four forms from among the forms of the prayer of fear:

The first: it is the one we mentioned just above, when the fear is intense and the fighting joins, so that none of them can abandon the fighting. They pray, as we mentioned, on foot and mounted, etc., the form.

The second: it is the one the Prophet ﷺ prayed at Batn Nakhl, namely that he prays with the first group their prayer in full, then all of them give the salam, the Imam and the followers. Then the other group, which had been facing the enemy, comes and he prays with them once more, which is an obligatory prayer for them and a voluntary one for him. The prayer at Batn Nakhl was narrated by Jabir and Abu Bakrah. As for the hadith of Jabir, Muslim narrated that he prayed with the Prophet ﷺ the prayer of fear, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rak'ahs with one of the two groups, then prayed two rak'ahs with the other group. So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed four rak'ahs and prayed two rak'ahs with each group.

al-Bukhari mentioned it in abridged form, and al-Shafi'i, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Khuzaymah narrated it through al-Hasan from Jabir, and in it he gave the salam after the first two rak'ahs, then prayed two rak'ahs with the other group.

As for the hadith of Abu Bakrah, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim and al-Daraqutni narrated it, and in one narration it is the Zuhr prayer, and in another narration it is the Maghrib prayer. Ibn al-Qattan's criticism of this hadith of Abu Bakrah, on the ground that he embraced Islam some time after the prayer of fear occurred, is rejected: even if we grant that he did not attend the prayer of fear, his hadith is a mursal of a Companion, and the mursal reports of the Companions have the ruling of the connected (mawsul), as is well known. Note that the hadith of Abu Bakrah does not state that this occurred at Batn Nakhl.

The Shafi'is have used the prayer at Batn Nakhl as evidence for the permissibility of the obligatory prayer being performed behind one performing a voluntary prayer (al-muftarid khalf al-mutanaffil).

Know that this manner, which we mentioned as the manner of the prayer of Batn Nakhl, is as al-Nawawi, Ibn Hajar and others have stated. Some narrations in Muslim's and al-Bukhari's collections and elsewhere indicate that it is the prayer of Dhat al-Riqa' (the Battle of Dhat al-Riqa'). Ibn Hajar was certain that they are two distinct prayers, and God knows best.

Some narrations also indicate that the prayer of Nakhl is the prayer of 'Usfan, and God knows best.

The third form, among the forms chosen by al-Shafi'i, is the prayer of 'Usfan. Its manner, as Jabir (may God be pleased with him) said, is: "I witnessed the prayer of fear with the Messenger of God (ﷺ). We formed two rows: one row behind the Messenger of God (ﷺ), with the enemy between us and the qiblah. The Prophet (ﷺ) said the takbir and we all said the takbir with him. He bowed and we all bowed. Then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised our heads. Then he went down into prostration, along with the row that was next to him, while the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Prophet (ﷺ) had completed the prostration and the row next to him had stood up, the rear row went down into prostration and then stood. Then the rear row advanced and the front row withdrew. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) bowed and we all bowed. Then he raised his head from bowing and we all raised our heads. Then he went down into prostration with the row next to him, which had been the rear row in the first rak'ah, while the rear row stood facing the enemy. When the Prophet (ﷺ) had completed the prostration along with the row next to him, the rear row went down into prostration and prostrated. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) gave the salam and we all gave the salam." This is the wording of Muslim in his Sahih. al-Nasa'i and al-Bayhaqi related it through the narration of Ibn 'Abbas, and Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Hibban and al-Hakim related it through the narration of Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi, whose name is Zayd ibn al-Samit, and he is a Companion. (p-258)

Ibn Hajar's statement in al-Taqrib, in the section on kunyas, that he was a Successor (tabi'i), is apparently a lapse on his part, may God have mercy on him. We said that this manner is among the manners chosen by al-Shafi'i, although it differs from the form that is authentically reported from him in the prayer of 'Usfan, because he instructed that the hadith be acted upon when it is authentic, and that this is his school. The form that is authentically reported from al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, in Mukhtasar al-Muzani and al-Umm, is that he said: The imam prays with them and bows and prostrates with them all, except for one row or part of a row which stands guard facing the enemy. When they stand up after the two prostrations, the row that is guarding them prostrates. When he bows, he bows with them all, and when he prostrates, those who were guarding first prostrate with him, except for one row or part of a row which guards them from among them. When they have performed two prostrations and sat, those who guarded prostrate, then they recite the tashahhud, then he gives the salam with them all together. This is close to the prayer of the Prophet (ﷺ) at 'Usfan. He said: If the row that was guarding withdrew to the second row and the second advanced and guarded, there is no harm. End of quotation, through al-Nawawi's transmission.

It appears that al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, holds that both forms, I mean the one we mentioned in the hadith of Jabir, Ibn 'Abbas and Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi, and the one we quoted from al-Shafi'i, are both permissible, and that following what is established in the Sahih is more worthy than other forms. The prayer of 'Usfan mentioned is the 'Asr prayer.

In some narrations in Abu Dawud and others, it has come that a form similar to the prayer of 'Usfan that we mentioned was also performed by him (ﷺ) on the day of Banu Sulaym.

The fourth form, among the forms chosen by al-Shafi'i (may God have mercy on him), is the prayer of Dhat al-Riqa'. The manner chosen by al-Shafi'i from it is the one we earlier cited as narrated by Malik from Yazid ibn Ruman, namely that the imam prays with the first group one rak'ah, then they leave him, complete their own prayer and give the salam, and go to face the enemy. He remains standing in the second rak'ah, prolonging the recitation until the others come, and he then prays the remaining rak'ah with them, and sits waiting for them until they complete their remaining rak'ah, then he gives the salam with them. We have already mentioned that Malik narrated this manner from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Salih ibn Khawwat ibn Jubayr, from one who prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ) the prayer of fear on the day of Dhat al-Riqa'. The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also related it through his chain: al-Bukhari related it from Qutaybah, from Malik, and Muslim from Yahya ibn Yahya, from Malik, approximately as we mentioned. We have also mentioned that Malik first stated this manner, then retracted it in favour of the view that the imam gives the salam without waiting for the second group to complete their prayer before he gives the salam with them.

The prayer of Dhat al-Riqa' has another manner, other than the one chosen by al-Shafi'i, and it is established in the two Sahihs through the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, who said: "The Messenger of God (ﷺ) prayed the prayer of fear with one of the two groups one rak'ah, while the other group faced the enemy. Then they withdrew and stood in the place of their companions, facing the enemy. Those others came, and the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed with them one rak'ah, then the Prophet (ﷺ) gave the salam. Then these completed one rak'ah and those completed one rak'ah." This is the wording of Muslim; al-Bukhari's wording is similar in meaning. The chains from Ibn 'Umar do not differ on this. Its apparent meaning is that they completed their prayers for themselves at one time, but it is also possible that they completed them in succession, and this is the preferred view in terms of meaning, because their completing together at one time would entail neglecting the required guarding and leaving the imam alone. This is supported by what Abu Dawud related from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, whose wording is: "Then he gave the salam, and these, that is the second group, stood and prayed one rak'ah for themselves, then gave the salam and departed, and those others returned to their place and prayed one rak'ah for themselves, then gave the salam." Its apparent meaning is that the second group separated their two rak'ahs by a gap, and then the first group completed after them. Know that what al-Rafi'i and others mention in the books of fiqh, namely that in this hadith of Ibn 'Umar the second group delayed, the first group came and completed one rak'ah, then they withdrew, and the second group returned and completed, is contrary to the established narrations in the two Sahihs and elsewhere.

Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath that he did not find this in any of the chains. As for Imam Ahmad (may God have mercy on him), all the types of the prayer of fear established from the Prophet (ﷺ) are permissible in his view, and the one he prefers among them is the prayer of Dhat al-Riqa', for which we have also already mentioned al-Shafi'i's choice. It is that the imam prays with the first group one rak'ah, then they complete their own prayer and give the salam and go to face the enemy; then the other group comes, and he prays with them the other rak'ah, then they pray one rak'ah, and when they have completed it and recited the tashahhud, he gives the salam with them.

* *
