His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾, the verse. He did not specify here any of their wishful thinking, nor any of the wishful thinking of the People of the Book, but He pointed to some of that in other passages,

• such as His saying concerning the false wishful thinking of the Arabs: ﴿And they say, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished"﴾ [Saba': 35],

• and His saying concerning them: ﴿There is only our worldly life, and we will not be resurrected﴾ [al-An'am: 29], and similar verses.

• And His saying concerning the wishful thinking of the People of the Book: ﴿And they say, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians." Those are their wishful thinkings﴾, the verse [al-Baqarah: 111],

• and His saying: ﴿And the Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved"﴾, the verse [al-Ma'idah: 18],

and similar verses.

As for what some scholars have mentioned, that the occasion of revelation of the verse was that the Muslims and the People of the Book boasted, and the People of the Book said: "Our Prophet came before your Prophet, and our Book came before your Book, so we have more right to Allah than you," and the Muslims said: "We have more right to Allah than you, our Prophet is the Seal of the Prophets, and our Book supersedes the books that came before it," so Allah revealed: ﴿Not by your wishful thinking﴾, the verse [al-Nisa': 123]. This does not contradict what we have mentioned, because the consideration is the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the occasion.

Almighty Allah said: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good?﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse, Allah mentions that there is no one better in religion than the one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good. This is because the interrogative of denial (istifham al-inkar, a rhetorical question expressing negation) carries the meaning of negation. In another place He explicitly stated that whoever is like this has grasped the firmest handhold, which is His saying: ﴿And whoever submits his face to Allah while he is a doer of good has grasped the most trustworthy handhold﴾ [Luqman: 22]. The meaning of submitting one's face to Allah is obeying Him, yielding to Him, and submitting to Allah the Exalted by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition, while being a doer of good (muhsin), that is, sincerely devoting his deeds to Allah without associating anything with Him, being mindful of Allah in them as if he sees Him. If he does not see Him, then Allah the Exalted sees him. The Arabs use the expression "submitting the face" and mean by it complete submission and surrender. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn Nufayl al-'Adawi:

I have submitted my face to Him to whom the clouds are subservient, bearing sweet, pure water.

I have submitted my face to Him to whom the earth is subservient, bearing heavy boulders.

(p. 313)

The Exalted's statement: ﴿And what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women﴾ and so on. He did not specify here what this is that is recited to them in the Book, but He specified it at the beginning of the surah, in His statement: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans, then marry from [other] women what seems good to you﴾ and so on [An-Nisa: 3], as we have already mentioned from the Mother of the Believers, 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her. So His statement here, ﴿And what is recited﴾ [An-Nisa: 127], is in the grammatical position of nominative (raf') as a conjunction (ma'tuf) upon the subject, which is the word "Allah." The sense is: ﴿Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them"﴾ [An-Nisa: 127], and also: what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women, and that is His statement: ﴿And if you fear that you will not act justly toward orphans﴾ and so on. The content of the ruling that this which is recited to us in the Book gives is the prohibition of depriving orphan girls of their rights. So whoever fears that he will not act justly toward the orphan girl in his guardianship, let him leave her and marry whatever other women seem good to him. This is the verified meaning of the verse, as we have mentioned. Accordingly, the omitted preposition in His statement ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ is "an" (from/away from). The sense is: you turn away from marrying them because of their little wealth and beauty, i.e., just as you turn away from marrying them if they are poor in wealth and beauty, so it is not lawful for you to marry them if they possess wealth and beauty except by acting justly toward them in their rights, as was reported earlier from 'Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

Some scholars said: the omitted preposition is "fi" (in). That is: you desire to marry them if they are endowed with beauty and abundance of wealth, while you do not act justly with them. Those who said it is a metaphor and differed over whether the word may be taken in its literal and metaphorical senses simultaneously permitted that in the rational metaphor (al-majaz al-'aqli), as in your saying: "Zayd and his giving have enriched me." Attributing the enriching to Zayd is a literal rational attribution, and attributing it to the giving is a rational metaphor, so it is permissible to combine them. Likewise, attributing the giving of a ruling to Allah is literal, and attributing it to what is recited is a rational metaphor according to them, because it is its cause; so it is permissible to combine the two.

Some scholars said: His statement ﴿And what is recited to you﴾ is in the genitive position (mahall jarr) as a conjunction upon the pronoun. Accordingly, the sense is: ﴿Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them"﴾ and He gives you a ruling concerning what is recited to you. This view is weakened by two matters:

First: that Allah usually gives a ruling concerning what is recited in this Book, and does not give a ruling concerning it, because its matter is evident.

Second: that conjunction upon a pronoun in the genitive without repeating the genitive particle was deemed weak by more than one of the scholars of Arabic. Ibn Malik permitted it, citing the reading of Hamza, "and the wombs" in the genitive, as a conjunction upon the pronoun in His statement ﴿by whom you ask one another﴾ [An-Nisa: 1], and by its occurrence in poetry, such as his statement:

"Today she has come close to reviling us and insulting us, so go away, what is wrong with you and the days, of wonder?"

Here "al-ayyam" (the days) is genitive by conjunction upon the kaf (you). A similar example is the statement of another:

"We hang our swords on the like of pillars, and what is between them and the ankle is a place of swinging, of stumbling."

Here "al-ka'b" (the ankle) is genitive by conjunction upon the pronoun before it. And the statement of another:

"He sought the horizons of the sky but found no ascent there, nor did the earth provide a seat."

So his statement "wa-la al-ard" (nor the earth), in the genitive, is a conjunction upon the pronoun. And the statement of another:

"I pass by the battalion, not knowing whether my death was in it or in something else."

So "siwaha" (something else) is in the genitive position by conjunction upon the pronoun.

It was answered regarding the verse that it may be an oath, and Allah has the right to swear by whatever He wills of His creation, just as He swore by all His creatures in His statement: ﴿So I swear by what you see﴾ ﴿and what you do not see﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 38-39]. And regarding the verses of poetry, that they are an anomaly to be preserved but not made a basis for analogy. Ibn al-Qayyim affirmed the permissibility of conjunction upon a genitive pronoun without repeating the genitive particle, and counted among it His statement: ﴿Allah is sufficient for you, and [for] those who follow you of the believers﴾ [Al-Anfal: 64]. He said that His statement "wa-man" (and [for] whoever) is in the genitive position by conjunction upon the genitive pronoun in His statement "hasbuka" (sufficient for you). The sense upon it is: ﴿Allah is sufficient for you﴾, i.e., sufficient for you and sufficient for whoever follows you of the believers. Ibn al-Qayyim and al-Qurtubi permitted that His statement ﴿and whoever follows you﴾ be in the accusative as a conjunction upon the position (mahall), since the kaf is in the genitive form but in the accusative position. A similar example is the statement of the poet:

"When war comes and the staffs are split, then sufficient for you, and al-Dahhak, is a keen-edged sword."

Here "al-Dahhak" is in the accusative, as we mentioned. Some scholars also counted among it His statement: ﴿And We placed for you therein means of livelihood, and [also] for those for whom you are not providers﴾ [Al-Hijr: 20]. They said: "wa-man" is a conjunction upon the pronoun of address in His statement "lakum" (for you), and the sense upon it is: We placed for you and for those for whom you are not providers therein means of livelihood. Likewise, the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of "wa-ma yutla" as a subject whose predicate is omitted, or whose predicate is "fi al-kitab" (in the Book), or as an accusative object of an omitted verb whose estimate is "and it makes clear to you what is recited," or as a genitive by being an oath, are all not apparent.

Some scholars said: what is meant by His statement ﴿and what is recited to you in the Book﴾ [An-Nisa: 127] is the verses of inheritance, because they used not to give inheritance to women, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about that, and Allah revealed the verses of inheritance.

According to this view, what clarifies His statement ﴿and what is recited to you in the Book﴾ is His statement: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [An-Nisa: 11], the two verses, and His statement at the end of the surah: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning al-kalalah"﴾ [An-Nisa: 176]. The apparent view is that the statement of the Mother of the Believers is more correct and more evident.

Reminder:

The verbal noun formed from "an" and its clause in His statement ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾ [An-Nisa: 127] originally is in the genitive by an omitted preposition. We have already mentioned the disagreement over whether it is "an" (from), which is the more evident, or "fi" (in). After removing the said genitive particle, the verbal noun is in the accusative position in verification. This is the view of al-Kisa'i and al-Khalil, and it is the more analogically sound, because the preposition is weak in governing when omitted.

Al-Akhfash said: it is in the genitive position by the omitted particle, as evidenced by the statement of the poet:

"I did not visit Layla for her being a beloved to me, nor for a debt owed to me that I seek from her."

Here "dayn" (debt) is in the genitive by conjunction upon the position of "an takuna" (that she be). That is: for her being a beloved, nor for a debt. Those who held the first view rejected the argument from this verse, saying it is a conjunction by mistaken analogy (ʿatf al-tawahhum), like the statement of Zuhayr:

"It became clear to me that I am not one who reaches what has passed, nor one who outstrips anything when it comes."

Here "sabiq" (one who outstrips) is in the genitive due to the mistaken expectation that the preposition "bi" enters upon the item conjoined to it, which is the predicate of "laysa" (is not). And the statement of another:

"Ill-omened ones who do not reform a tribe, nor any caller except with the separation of its crow."

Here "na'iq" (caller) is in the genitive due to the mistaken expectation of "bi." Know that the genitive particle is not regularly omitted except in the verbal noun formed from "an." Sibawayh permitted both forms. Their clause, according to the majority, is as stated, contrary to 'Ali ibn Sulayman al-Akhfash, who said that it is regular in everything when there is no ambiguity. Ibn Malik set this in his al-Kafiyah with the verse:

"Ibn Sulayman saw its regularity, if no ambiguity is feared, like 'the man whom Zayd has gone far from.'"

When the genitive particle is omitted with other than "an" and "an" in transmitted usage according to the majority's view, and by analogy according to al-Akhfash's view when there is no ambiguity, then the accusative is required. The governing element according to the Basrans is the verb, and according to the Kufans it is the removal of the governing particle, as in his statement:

"You pass by the abodes and you will not deviate, your speech to me is then forbidden."

Its retention in the genitive with the particle omitted is anomalous, as in the statement of al-Farazdaq:

"When it is said: which of the people is the worst tribe? The fingers point with palms toward Kulayb."

That is: the fingers point with the palms, i.e., together with the palms, toward Kulayb.

His statement: ﴿And that you stand up for orphans with justice﴾ and so on. "Al-qist" means justice. He did not specify here the justice which He commanded for the orphans, but He indicated it in other places, such as:

• His statement: ﴿And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the way that is best﴾ [Al-An'am: 152],

• and His statement: ﴿Say, "Improving their condition is best. And if you mix your affairs with them, they are your brothers. And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer"﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 220],

• and His statement: ﴿As for the orphan, do not oppress [him]﴾ [Ad-Duha: 9],

• and His statement: ﴿And gave wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives and orphans﴾ and so on [Al-Baqarah: 177],

and similar verses. All of that contains the upholding of justice toward orphans.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 128:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And souls are made to be present with greed﴾, and so on. In this noble verse, He, exalted is He, mentions that souls have been made to be present with greed, meaning that it is made something present for them, as though it constantly accompanies them and never leaves them, because they were created with it (jubilat).

In another place He indicates that no one attains success unless Allah protects him from the greed of his own soul, and this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And whoever is protected from the greed of his own soul, it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr: 9]. The implication of the conditional clause is that whoever is not protected from the greed of his soul does not attain success, and this is so. Some scholars restricted it to the greed that leads to withholding the rights which the Sharia requires, or which manliness (muruwwah) demands. When greed reaches that point, it is miserliness (bukhl), and it is a vice (radhilah). And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 129:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives, even if you should strive to do so﴾. This justice which He, may He be exalted, mentions here as being impossible to achieve is justice in love and natural inclination, because it is not within the power of human beings. This is unlike justice in the legal rights, which is achievable. He, may He be exalted, indicated this with His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not deal justly [with the orphan girls], then marry those that please you of [other] women, two or three or four. But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one or those your right hands possess. That is more suitable that you not incline [to injustice]﴾ [An-Nisa: 3], meaning: that you not act unjustly in the legal rights. The Arabs say: "ʿala yaʿulu" when one acts unjustly and deviates, and he is ʿaʾil (one who deviates). From this is the saying of Abu Talib: [Tawil]

By a balance of justice that does not cheat by a single grain, for it has a witness from itself, not deviating (ʿaʾil).

That is: not deviating and not unjust. From this is the saying of another: [Basit]

They said: "We followed the Messenger of God," and they cast aside the saying of the Messenger and acted unjustly (ʿalu) in the scales.

That is: they acted unjustly. And the saying of another: [Wafir]

Three souls and three camels, indeed time has been unjust (ʿala) to my dependants.

That is: it acted unjustly and deviated. As for the saying of Uhayhah ibn al-Julah al-Ansari: [Wafir]

The poor man does not know when his wealth will come, and the rich man does not know when he will become poor (yaʿil).

And the saying of Jarir: [Kamil]

God has sent down in the Book an obligation for the wayfarer and for the needy dependant (al-ʿaʾil).

And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He found you poor and made you self-sufficient﴾ [Ad-Duha: 8]. All of that derives from al-ʿaylah, which is poverty. From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you fear poverty﴾ [At-Tawbah: 28], and so ʿala meaning "acted unjustly" is from the root with waw in the middle, while that meaning "became poor" is from the root with ya' in the middle.

Al-Shafiʿi, may God have mercy on him, said: The meaning of His saying: ﴿that you not ʿaulu﴾ [An-Nisa: 3] is that your dependants become numerous, from "ʿala al-rajulu yaʿulu" when his dependants became numerous. The saying of some of them that this is not sound, and that what is heard is aʿala al-rajula in the fourth form on the pattern of afʿala, so he is muʿil when his dependants are many, has no basis; for al-Shafiʿi is among the people most knowledgeable of the Arabic language, and because ʿala meaning "his dependants became numerous" is the dialect of Himyar. From it is the saying of the poet: [Wafir]

Indeed death seizes every living being without doubt, even if he walks (or is wealthy) and has many dependants (ʿala).

That is: even if his livestock and dependants become numerous. And Talhah ibn Musarrif recited the verse as ﴿that you not uʿilu﴾ with a dammah on the ta', from aʿala, meaning "his dependants became numerous," according to the well-known dialect.

Allah's saying: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾. In this noble verse He mentions that if the spouses separate, Allah enriches each one of them from His abundance and His vast bounty, and He links the two matters by making one of them a condition and the other a consequence.

He has also mentioned that marriage is a cause of wealth, in His saying: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous of your male servants and your female servants. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾ [an-Nur: 32].

"His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others﴾, the verse. In this noble verse Allah, the Exalted, mentions that if He wills He can remove the people who exist at the time of its revelation and bring others in their place. He establishes the proof for this in another place, and that proof is that He removed those who were before them and brought them in their place. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and cause to succeed you whatever He wills, as He produced you from the descendants of another people﴾ [al-An'am: 133].

He also mentions in another place that if they turn away, He will replace them with others, and that those who are substituted will not be like those they replace, but will be better than them. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you﴾ [Muhammad: 38].

He also mentions in another place that this is easy for Him and not difficult. This is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation﴾ ﴿And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ [Ibrahim: 19, 20], meaning: it is not impossible for Him nor hard."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 139:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do they seek honour with them? Indeed, honour belongs entirely to Allah﴾. In this noble verse He mentions that all honour belongs to Him, may He be majestic and exalted.

(p-319) And in another place He explains that the honour which belongs to Him alone is the honour with which He honoured His Messenger and the believers, and that is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And honour belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 8]. That is, it is by Allah's bestowing honour upon them. And 'izzah (honour, might) means victory (al-ghalabah). From it is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and he overcame me in the argument﴾ [Sad: 23], that is, he overpowered me in the dispute. And among the sayings of the Arabs is "whoever is mighty plunders" (man 'azza bazz), meaning whoever overcomes, seizes spoils. From it is the saying of al-Khansa': [Metre: al-Mutaqarib]

As though they had never been a protected refuge to be feared, when people, at that time, whoever was mighty plundered.

The Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 140:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And He has already sent down to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in a conversation other than that; indeed, you would then be like them﴾. This ruling to which He refers here is the one mentioned in Surah al-An'am, in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when you see those who engage in vain talk concerning Our verses, turn away from them until they engage in a conversation other than that﴾ [al-An'am: 68]. His saying here, ﴿do not sit with them﴾, does not clarify the ruling for the case where they forget the prohibition and so sit with them. However, He clarified it in al-An'am with His saying: ﴿And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-An'am: 68].

**Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 141:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾, there are several opinions among the scholars regarding the meaning of this verse:

Among them: the meaning is "And Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers on the Day of Resurrection." This is narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib and Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them. It is supported by His saying at the beginning of the verse: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers﴾ to the end of the verse [An-Nisa: 141], and this is evident. Ibn ʿAtiyyah said: "All the people of ta'wil (interpretation) held this view," as al-Qurtubi transmitted from him. Ibn al-ʿArabi regarded it as weak, claiming that the end of the verse does not refer back to its beginning.

Among them: the meaning of "He will not give them a way over the believers" is that He will not let them destroy the dominion of the Muslims, uproot them, or seize their territory (bayḍah), as established in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere from the Prophet (ﷺ), in the hadith of Thawban, that he said: "I asked my Lord that He not destroy my Ummah with a general famine, and that He not let an enemy from outside themselves overpower them so that it seizes their territory. Allah granted me that for my Ummah, so that some of them will destroy others and some of them will take others captive." Many verses support this view, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, We will surely support Our messengers and those who believe in the worldly life﴾ [Ghafir: 51], His saying: ﴿And it was incumbent upon Us to support the believers﴾ [Ar-Rum: 47], and His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors upon the earth, as He made successors those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them and will surely replace their fear with security, [saying], "They will worship Me, not associating anything with Me"﴾ [An-Nur: 55], among other verses.

Among them: the meaning is that He will not give them a way over the believers, except that they enjoin one another in falsehood, do not forbid one another from wrongdoing, and hold back from repentance, so that the empowering of the enemy over them comes from themselves, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whatever disaster strikes you is because of what your hands have earned﴾ [Ash-Shura: 30].

Ibn al-ʿArabi said: "This is extremely precious, and in meaning it returns to the first view, for they are victorious if they obey, and the calamity came to them from themselves in both cases."

Among them: He will not give them a way over the believers by legislation (shar'an); if such a way is found, it is contrary to the Shariʿah.

Among them: the meaning of "way" (sabil) is proof (ḥujjah, argument), that is: He will not give them a proof over the believers. This is clarified by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they bring you no example except that We bring you the truth and better explanation﴾ [Al-Furqan: 33]. Some scholars derived from this noble verse the prohibition of the disbeliever's lasting ownership of a Muslim slave, and Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 142:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And when they stand up to prayer, they stand up lazily, showing off to the people, and they do not remember Allah except a little﴾. In this noble verse He explains the description of the prayer of the hypocrites: that they stand up to it in laziness and ostentation, and that they do not remember Allah in it except a little. A similar verse condemning them for their negligence regarding prayer is His saying: ﴿And they do not come to prayer except while they are lazy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 54], and His saying: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'un: 4–5]. From the implication of the opposite (mafhum al-mukhalafah, the reasoning by contrast) of these verses it is understood that the prayer of the sincere believers is not like this. This implication Allah has stated explicitly in many verses, by His saying: ﴿Certainly the believers have succeeded, who are humble in their prayer﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 1–2],

• and His saying: ﴿And those who are careful over their prayers﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 9],

• and His saying: ﴿There glorify Him in the mornings and the evenings men whom neither commerce nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah and the establishment of prayer﴾ [al-Nur: 36–37],

and other verses besides these.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 145:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire﴾ — the verse. In this noble verse He mentions that the hypocrites are in the lowest levels of the Fire, seeking refuge with Allah, exalted is He.

(p-321) And He mentions in another place that the people of Pharaoh on the Day of Resurrection will be commanded to be made to enter the most severe punishment, and that is His statement: ﴿And on the Day the Hour is established: "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the most severe punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46].

And He mentions in another place that He will punish those among the companions of the Table who disbelieved with a punishment He will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds, and that is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Allah said, "Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds."﴾ And He mentions in another place that He will punish those among the companions of the Table who disbelieved with a punishment He will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds, and that is His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Allah said, "Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves after that among you, I will surely punish him with a punishment I will not inflict upon anyone among the worlds."﴾

[Al-Ma'idah: 115]. These verses clarify that the most severely punished people of the Fire are the hypocrites, the people of Pharaoh, and those among the companions of the Table who disbelieved, as Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said. And "al-darak" with a fatha or a sukun on the ra' are two well-known dialects and two canonical recitations (qira'at sab'iyyah).

The Words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then you took the calf [for worship] after clear proofs had come to you, but We pardoned you for that﴾ — the verse. Here He did not explain the reason for His pardoning them for the sin of taking the calf as a god, but He explained it in Surat al-Baqarah with His words: ﴿So repent to your Creator and kill yourselves; that is better for you in the sight of your Creator. Then He accepted your repentance. Indeed, He is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 54].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 154:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We said to them, "Do not transgress in the Sabbath"﴾ [the verse], he did not clarify here whether they complied with this command, so that they abstained from transgression on the Sabbath or not. However, he clarified in other places that they did not comply, and that they transgressed on the Sabbath, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you had already known those among you who transgressed in the Sabbath﴾ [the verse] [al-Baqarah: 65], and His saying: ﴿And ask them about the town which was by the sea, when they transgressed in the Sabbath﴾ [the verse] [al-A'raf: 163].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 156:

God's words: ﴿And for their disbelief and their speaking against Mary a tremendous slander﴾. Here He did not explain this tremendous slander which they uttered against the truthful one (al-Siddiqah), Mary the virgin. However, He indicated in another place that it was their accusing her of immorality (al-fahishah), and that she had brought a child not born of legitimate lineage (li-ghayr rishdah), according to their false claim, may God curse them. This is in His words: ﴿Then she brought him to her people, carrying him. They said, "O Mary, you have certainly brought something unprecedented (shay'an fariyyan)!"﴾ [Maryam: 27], meaning the commission of immorality. ﴿O sister of Aaron, your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste (baghiyyan)﴾ [Maryam: 28], i.e., a fornicator. "How then could you commit immorality when your parents are not like that?" In the narration, they accused her of (being involved with) Yusuf the carpenter, who was among the righteous. Slander (buhtan) is the most severe form of lying, the kind that is considered astonishing.

﴿Because of the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things that had been lawful for them﴾ (p-322). He did not specify here which good things He made unlawful for them because of their wrongdoing, but He specified them in Surat al-An'am, saying: ﴿And to those who were Jews We made unlawful every animal with claws, and of the cattle and sheep We made unlawful to them their fat, except what their backs or their entrails carry, or what is mixed with bone. That was their recompense for their rebellion, and indeed We are truthful﴾ [al-An'am: 146].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 165:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾, and the rest of the verse. Here He does not specify what this argument would have been, which people would have had against Him had He punished them without warning them through the tongues of the messengers. However, He clarified it in Surah "Ta-Ha" with His saying: ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before this, they would have said, "Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger, so we could have followed Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 134]. He alluded to it in Surah "al-Qasas" with His saying: ﴿And if not that a disaster should strike them for what their hands have put forth, they would say, "Our Lord, if only You had sent to us a messenger, so we could have followed Your verses and been among the believers"﴾ [al-Qasas: 47].

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 171:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess (ghuluww) in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth﴾. The excess (ghuluww) that they were forbidden from, and the saying of what is not the truth, is the saying of some of them that Isa is the son of Allah, the saying of some of them that he is Allah, and the saying of some of them that he is a god along with Allah. Allah, glorified and exalted is He above all of that, exceedingly high. This is shown by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 30], and His saying: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, son of Mary"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 17], and His saying: ﴿They have certainly disbelieved who say, "Indeed, Allah is the third of three"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 73]. Here He pointed to the refutation of these fabrications by His saying: ﴿The Messiah, Isa son of Mary, is only the messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Nisa': 171],

• and His saying: ﴿The Messiah will never be too proud to be a servant of Allah﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Nisa': 172],

• and His saying: ﴿The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; no doubt messengers had passed on before him, and his mother was a supremely truthful woman; they both used to eat food﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 75],

• and His saying: ﴿Say, "Who could prevent Allah at all if He intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother and everyone on earth entirely?"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 17].

Some scholars said: The excess and the saying of what is not the truth that is forbidden in this verse also includes what they said of slander against Mary, and al-Qurtubi (al-Qurtubi, the tafsir scholar) adopted this view. According to it, the forbidden excess includes both neglect (tafrit) and overstepping (ifrat).

The scholars have established that the truth lies between neglect and overstepping, and this is the meaning of the saying of Mutarrif ibn Abdullah: "The good deed is between two bad deeds." By this you know that whoever avoids both neglect and overstepping has been guided. Indeed, one who said it spoke well, in the tawil meter:

"Do not go to excess in any matter, but moderate; for both extremes of the course of affairs are blameworthy."

It is established in the Sahih from him (ﷺ) that he said: "Do not overpraise me as the Christians overpraised Isa son of Mary. Say: the servant of Allah and His messenger."

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And His word which He directed to Mary and a spirit from Him﴾. The word "min" (from) in this verse is not partitive (lil-tab'id), as the Christians claim in fabrication against Allah. Rather, "min" here indicates the starting point (li-ibtida' al-ghayah), meaning: the origin of that spirit with which Isa was born alive is from Allah, the Exalted, because He is the One who gave him life through it. What shows that "min" here indicates the starting point is His saying: ﴿And He subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth, all of it from Him﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 13], meaning: the origin of all of that is from Him, exalted is He. What supports what we have mentioned is what is related from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he said: "Allah created the spirits of the children of Adam when He took the covenant from them, then He returned them to the loins of Adam, and He kept with Him the spirit of Isa, peace be upon him. When He intended to create him, He sent that spirit to Mary, and from it came Isa, peace be upon him." This idafah (attribution) is one of honor, because all spirits are from His creation, exalted is He, like His saying: ﴿And purify My House for those who circumambulate﴾ [al-Hajj: 26], and His saying: ﴿The she-camel of Allah﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Shams: 13].

It was also said: The one from whom wondrous things appear is sometimes called a spirit and is attributed to Allah, so it is said: "This is a spirit from Allah," meaning: from His creation. Isa used to heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead to life by Allah's permission, so he deserved this name. It was also said: he was called a spirit because of the breath of Jibril, peace be upon him, mentioned in the surah of "al-Anbiya'" and "al-Tahrim." The Arabs call breath a spirit, because it is wind that comes out of the spirit (rih). From this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah:

"I said to him: lift it up to yourself and revive it with your spirit, and blow into it a blowing that is measured."

According to this view, His saying ﴿and a spirit﴾ is coordinated (ma'tuf) with the pronoun referring to Allah, who is the subject of "alqaha" (He directed it), as al-Qurtubi said. And Allah knows best.

Some scholars said: ﴿and a spirit from Him﴾ means: a mercy from Him, and Isa was a mercy from Allah to whoever followed him. It was said that from this is: ﴿and He supported them with a spirit from Him﴾ [al-Anfal: 22], meaning: with a mercy from Him. Al-Qurtubi also related this. It was also said: "a spirit from Him" means: a proof from Him, and Isa was a proof and a argument against his people (p-324). And knowledge is with Allah, the Exalted.

Allah's statement: ﴿And We have sent down to you a clear light﴾. The clear light here refers to the Great Qur'an, because it removes the darkness of ignorance and doubt just as physical light removes the darkness of night. Allah has clarified this in His statement: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit from Our command. You did not know what the Book was, nor what faith was; but We made it a light﴾ [ash-Shura: 52], and His statement: ﴿And follow the light which has been sent down with him﴾ [al-A'raf: 157], and similar verses.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿If there are two sisters, then they shall have two-thirds of what he leaves﴾, the verse. In this noble verse He stated that two sisters inherit two-thirds. What is meant by "the two" is two sisters not from the same mother, whether they are full sisters (shaqiqatayn) or paternal sisters (li-ab), by the consensus (ijma' (scholarly consensus)) of the scholars. He did not explain here the inheritance of three or more sisters, but He indicated in another place that sisters do not exceed two-thirds, however many they may be. This is His saying, may He be exalted, concerning daughters: ﴿And if they are women more than two, then for them are two-thirds of what he leaves﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]. It is known that daughters are closer in kinship (amass rahiman) and stronger in cause (aqwa sababan) for inheritance than sisters. So if they do not exceed two-thirds even when they are many, then likewise sisters, a fortiori (min bab awla). Most of the scholars of the foundations of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh) hold that fahwa al-khitab (the implicit meaning of the speech), that is, mafhum al-muwafaqa (the implication of agreement), in which the unmentioned case is more deserving of the ruling than the mentioned one, is from the category of the indication of the wording (dalalat al-lafz), not from the category of analogy (qiyas), contrary to al-Shafi'i and a group. Likewise the equivalent cases (al-masawi) on verification. So His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So do not say to them, "Uff"﴾ [al-Isra': 23] implies, a fortiori, the prohibition of striking them. And His saying: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾, to the end of the verse [al-Zalzalah: 7], implies, a fortiori, that whoever does the weight of a mountain of good or evil will see it. And His saying: ﴿And bring to witness two just men from among you﴾ [al-Talaq: 2] implies, a fortiori, the acceptance of the testimony of three or four just persons, for example. His prohibition, may blessings and peace be upon him (ﷺ), against sacrificing a one-eyed animal (al-awra') implies, a fortiori, the prohibition against sacrificing a blind animal (al-amya'). Likewise in the case of equivalents: the prohibition of consuming the property of an orphan implies by equivalence the prohibition of burning it and drowning it. His prohibition, may blessings and peace be upon him (ﷺ), against urinating in still water implies likewise the prohibition against urinating into a vessel and pouring it into it. His saying, may blessings and peace be upon him (ﷺ): "Whoever frees his share in a slave..." the hadith [and so on]. It implies likewise that a female slave is the same. There is no dispute over this among the majority of scholars, and only some of the Zahiriyyah (Literalists) differed on it.

It is known that their disagreement on such a matter has no weight. By this you know that when He, may He be exalted, stated explicitly that daughters, however many they may be, have no more than two-thirds, it is known that sisters are likewise, a fortiori. And knowledge is with Allah, may He be exalted.
